method_and_limits: measure_video.py keeps NUMBERS only: no footage and no per-frame skeleton is stored.
One camera angle only (front 3/4). 2D elbow angles are the primary read; 3D angles are biased for this motion and are recorded but not used (see assessment).

Alternating arms: only the picked (right) side's cycles are measured. The unpicked side's flexed 2D values (57-66 deg interior) are higher because that arm is farther from the camera and partly occluded; they were checked in a detail pass and are not used.

Upper-arm elevation (arm_elev) and torso lean were NOT measured from this clip (the tool reports elbow/knee/hip only); the animation comparison for those metrics uses the provisional gate bounds and visual inspection, stated as such in the report.

published_data.statement: No peer-reviewed study giving a peak elbow-flexion angle for a standard standing dumbbell curl was found in this search (12-15 Nov 2026). The curl comparison therefore rests on the measured clip plus the AAOS envelope, and the report states this plainly instead of inventing a literature target.

purpose: Measured reference for the provisional Dumbbell Curl animation: one licensed video clip measured with MediaPipe, plus the best published elbow-range data found. Evaluation record only: this file does not make the animation approved.

reference_clips.assessment: TRUSTED: elbow 2D angles. Flexed (tool 'bottom' event): 2D median 50.1 deg interior (129.9 deg flexion), per-rep 48.6-50.4, confirmed by a multi-frame detail pass (right-side flexed-window medians 49.2-52.3) and by visual inspection of a landmark overlay (shoulder/elbow/wrist landmarks sit on the joints). Extended (tool 'top' event): 2D median 174.6 deg interior. DO NOT USE the 3D elbow values: flexed 3D median 86.8 deg interior (93 deg flexion) systematically understates flexion because monocular depth estimation compresses the forward-moving forearm; the 2D-3D gap (~37 deg) is a measurement artifact, not a range. NOTE on the tool's naming: for curls the 'top' event is arms EXTENDED and the 'bottom' event is arms FLEXED (the wrist signal is inverted vs presses); down_s (median 1.24 s) is the curl-up (concentric) phase and up_s (median 2.04 s) is the lowering (eccentric) phase. Knee/hip values (~170 deg) confirm a stable standing posture with no visible lean or dip.
reference_clips.author: Your Move (ymove.app)
reference_clips.camera: static, front 3/4 view, full body head-to-toe, white studio background
reference_clips.license: YMove royalty-free commercial use; credit required ('Exercise video by Your Move' with a link to ymove.app); no resale or redistribution as a standalone video library. Only measurements kept; no footage stored in this repository.
reference_clips.tool: pipeline/measure_video.py, MediaPipe Pose Landmarker heavy (Apache 2.0), --joint wrist, right side (visibility 1.00); alternating arms give 3 measured cycles for the picked side
reference_clips.variant_note: HAMMER (neutral-grip), ALTERNATING curls — not a supinated bilateral curl. Elbow flexion/extension range of motion is directly comparable to the animation's curl; forearm rotation (supination) differs and is NOT compared. The comparison uses elbow ROM and torso stability only. No standing supinated dumbbell curl clip with full-body static framing was found across Pexels, Wikimedia Commons, MIT OCW, Mixkit, Coverr and Pixabay searches (see rejected list); this is the closest licensed match and the variant difference is recorded here rather than hidden.
